sources.title: The current state of archaeology in Bashkiria and the Southern Urals
sources.note: HUN-REN regional synthesis: Karayakupovo chronology, Cis- and Trans-Ural variants, polyethnic caution, and mixed Ugric and Turkic-associated horizons.

sources.title: On the Beginnings of the Formation of the Bashkir Language
sources.note: Peer-reviewed historical-linguistic argument against projecting a homogeneous Bashkir-speaking community before the thirteenth century.

sources.title: Bashkir beliefs and Ibn Fadlan
sources.note: HUN-REN study identifying the 922 account as the first detailed record and separating observation, report, and misunderstanding.

sources.title: Chronology and Periodization of Uelgi Burial Ground
sources.note: Radiocarbon and artifact chronology placing the earliest Uyelgi complexes around the turn of the ninth century and the early group mainly in the ninth century.

sources.title: Ethnocultural Situation in the Trans-Urals in the Early 2nd Millennium AD: Evidence from Kurgan 11 at Uyelgi
sources.note: Russian Academy of Sciences archaeological study identifying at least four cultural horizons and mixed Southern Ural, Srostki, Altai, and Ugric-associated material.

sources.title: The Uyelgi Burial Complex, Ninth to Eleventh Centuries, in the Southern Trans-Urals
sources.note: HUN-REN and partner-institution excavation monograph covering Uyelgi fieldwork from 2009-2019 and 2021-2023 and the cemetery sequence across the ninth to eleventh centuries.

sources.title: Sixth Russian-Hungarian Ural Archaeological Expedition
sources.note: University fieldwork report on Kushnarenkovo archaeology, disturbed burials, excavation methods, and mixed nomadic and forest-steppe influences.

sources.title: History of Bashkortostan from Ancient Times to the 1860s
sources.note: Regional scholarly history contrasting the ninth-century Ibn Khordadbeh recension, which lacks Bashkirs, with al-Idrisi’s later version of Sallam’s journey.

sources.title: Muslim Sources on the Magyars in the Second Half of the Ninth Century
sources.note: Critical source study on layered geographic traditions, Sallam, Jayhani, and the ambiguity between Bashghird and Magyar labels.

sources.title: History of Civilizations of Central Asia, Volume IV
sources.note: UNESCO synthesis on the late ninth-century Oghuz-Khazar defeat of Pechenegs and the uncertain Bajgird identification.

sources.title: The Oghuz-Pecheneg Battles in the Eighth and Ninth Centuries
sources.note: University of Szeged study dating the recorded Oghuz occupation of Pecheneg Volga-Ural lands around 893-894 while questioning a simple Khazar alliance narrative.

sources.title: Muslim Coins as a Commodity and Means of Payment in the Volga-Ural Region
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of eighth- to early eleventh-century coin movement and the changing roles of Khazar and Volga Bulgar exchange.

sources.title: Reconstruction of Horse Equipment and Costume of the Southern Trans-Urals in the Ninth to Eleventh Centuries
sources.note: Artifact reconstruction from Uyelgi and Sineglazovo: harness, stirrups, bits, plaques, beads, headdress fittings, and a child burial belt.

sources.title: Early medieval genetic data from Ural region evaluated in the light of archaeological evidence of ancient Hungarians
sources.note: Peer-reviewed ancient-DNA analysis of Uyelgi chronological horizons and genetic continuity, used with an explicit warning that ancestry does not determine ethnicity.

sources.title: Mission to the Volga
sources.note: Library of Arabic Literature critical Arabic-English edition of Ibn Fadlan’s 921-922 journey and Yaqut’s preserved excerpts.

sources.title: On the route of the Baghdad embassy to Volga Bulgaria
sources.note: Institute of Steppe reconstruction placing the Bashghird encounter around 3 May 922 and arrival among the Volga Bulgars on 12 May.

sources.title: The worst of all Turkish peoples: Ibn Fadlan’s travel account as British naval intelligence
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of Ibn Fadlan’s outsider rhetoric, manuscript afterlife, ethnographic authority, and later stereotyping.

sources.title: Bashghird in medieval Arabic geographical writing
sources.note: Academic edition discussing the Arabic ethnonym Bāshghird, variant readings, and uncertainty in representing foreign names.

sources.title: Glottolog 5.2: Bashkir
sources.note: Current scholarly catalog entry for the modern Bashkir language, used only for present-day continuity and classification.

sources.title: Written sources in the Bashkir language of the late nineteenth and early twentieth century
sources.note: Russian Academy of Sciences linguistic study locating a substantial Bashkir-language written corpus much later than this card’s interval.

sources.title: Trade of Volga Bulgaria in the ninth to thirteenth centuries
sources.note: Russian Academy of Sciences archaeological synthesis of exchange objects, craft, agriculture, livestock, and routes reaching the Urals and Trans-Urals.

sources.title: The Bashkir Ural
sources.note: UNESCO description of the western Southern Urals, river valleys, karst, forests, and continuing wild-hive beekeeping traditions.

sources.title: Mountainous Urals Biosphere Reserve
sources.note: UNESCO description of mountain taiga, mixed forest, valleys, lakes, and current environmental diversity.

sources.title: The Ural Mountains and Human Origins
sources.note: UNESCO regional dossier noting long-lived wild-hive beekeeping in present Bashkortostan, used as regional evidence without assigning it to every ninth-century household.
